title: Storefront vacancy tax
summary: A yearly tax on ground-floor storefronts left empty for over a year.

decider.body: North Carolina General Assembly, then Chapel Hill Town Council
how: North Carolina towns can levy only the taxes the General Assembly authorizes, so a state law would have to allow it first.
Town staff would then draft an ordinance, and residents comment at a public hearing.
Town Council votes on the ordinance.

evidence.claim: San Francisco (2022) and Washington DC tax vacant storefronts; neither has a causal evaluation yet
NC towns can levy only taxes the General Assembly authorizes
evidence.source: UNC School of Government, local government finance

pros: Holding a storefront empty costs more, so landlords have reason to lower asking rents and lease more spaces.
Brings in some revenue from spaces that stay empty.
cons: Needs a change in state law before the Town could adopt it.
Neither city with such a tax (San Francisco since 2022, Washington DC) has a study of its effect yet.
